Jason La Canfora: Bobby Wagner will get a new deal before Russell Wilson

I get that maybe it'll be easier to find a number for Wagner that is acceptable for both parties before they find one for Russell, but can any Seahawks fans enlighten me as to why the organization seems so resistant to extend a mid round QB who has taken their organization to two Superbowls on his rookie contract and has unreal W-L numbers? Success in this league is practically only dictated by the quality of your quarterback and there are very few teams that have a QB you can confidently say deserve franchise money (Dalton contracts aside, of course)
Rumor is it is not the amount that is the issue, but the guaranteed percentage, that he wants 80%+ of his contract guaranteed.

I think I can provide a bit of context, with emphasis on the think part because nobody really.knows what's actually going on in the discussions.

First, a lot of the arguments I see people making about what Wilson should be signed for basically boil down to "that's just how it's done." While the status quo is quo for a reason, Pete Carroll and John Schneider have founded much of their current success on thinking and making moves outside the box. They found value by utilizing players with undervalued skillsets in unique ways. Look specifically at the recent tall cb renaissance brought about in large part by the success of Sherman. I would also point to what they're trying to do with the o-line, albeit with mixed results. For this reason, when you look at their track record, I think you need to throw out the conventional wisdom when you look at their decision making process.

So outside of conventional wisdom, what reasons are there to re-sign Wilson? Well, there's a lot. He's a fantastic player, and there's no question he adds a lot of value to the team. But does he add as much value as Graham and Lynch combined? (Or any other combination of players) Maybe he does, honestly, but maybe he doesn't. It is, after all, a run first offense with an o-line that will likely never be better than mediocre in pass protection. Honestly, Wilson's mobility is a perfect fit for this system, but this is also a team that throws among the least in the league. Couldn't thus be a place to save value? Seattle's offense is built around a strong rushing attack, and that's not going to change any time soon.

I've gotten away from my point a bit. The bottom line is that Seattle knows they have a franchise QB on their hands, and they have an idea of how much that's worth to them. They'd like to get a deal done, but given that they can franchise Russel they've got little reason to budge on that number and not a lot of urgency.

I've got more thoughts on the matter, but this post has grown long so I'll leave it there.
